label: a6-retry1-ex-locally-finite-versus-point-finite-families
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN
BOUNDARY: Checked the behaviour at x=0, at points inside intervals, at endpoints like 1/n, and at points outside the union. Every neighbourhood of 0 contains some (‑ε, ε) and therefore contains (0, ε), which contains I_n for all sufficiently large n (since 1/n → 0). Hence 0 has no neighbourhood meeting only finitely many members. Each point belongs to at most one interval, so the family is point‑finite. Actively searched for a counterexample (e.g., a neighbourhood of 0 meeting only finitely many, or a point belonging to infinitely many); none exists. The witness is robust.
SOURCES: Inspected the full text of `def-cover-refinement-and-local-finiteness` and `def-interval`. Their definitions of point‑finite, locally finite, and interval directly support the example. The cited Wikipedia reference is non‑load‑bearing.
CHECKED: Read the title, the example statement, the proof sketch, and the concluding remark. All are mathematically correct.
